text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** The comparison pages in your search results broadly agree on this. I'm going by their summaries and haven't opened the full articles.

| | LiFePO4 | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Cycle life** | About 3,000–6,000 cycles | About 1,000–2,000 cycles |
| **Safety** | More thermally stable and less prone to thermal runaway | Fine when well managed, but less heat-tolerant |
| **Weight and size** | Heavier and bulkier | About 20% lighter for the same capacity |
| **Cost** | Usually costs more per unit up front, but less per cycle over its life | Cheaper up front on some models |
| **Best for** | Home backup, RVs, off-grid and solar, daily use | Camping, travel, and uses where weight matters most |

**Choose LiFePO4 if:**
- You'll use it often, or keep it for home backup or an RV. At one cycle a day, 3,000+ cycles is roughly 8–10 years.
- It will sit in a garage, car, or hot environment.
- You want the lowest cost over its whole life.

**Choose NMC if:**
- You'll carry it a lot, for example backpacking, flights, or tailgating, and weight matters more than longevity.
- You only use it a few times a year and want a lower price or a lighter unit.

**Market trend:** One of the sources (Enough Watts) says all 54 power stations in its data set use LiFePO4. NMC is now mostly found in ultra-portable or older models, so you'll likely end up with LFP anyway. Check the spec sheet to confirm, because the chemistry is usually listed there.

**Example LiFePO4 unit:** The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a ~2 kWh class unit that suits home backup. One listing shows it at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF. That comes from a deal site's affiliate link, and I haven't verified the code. Confirm the price and chemistry at checkout.
